text:
maya: Heads-up — starting a 10% traffic cutover to model v2 for the recommendations endpoint, rolling over 30m. Want to pin cost/latency gates so we can auto-stop if things degrade. Any objections?
joel: +1, agree we need runtime checks. What exact gates do we want? latency p95, error rate, and token-cost-per-request?
anita: I'd add a per-tenant daily spend delta too — we saw a single tenant blow past budget during the last canary.
luo: We should decide where to evaluate these: router (edge) or control plane. Router gives fastest reaction but limited context (no spend history). Control plane can use tenant budget but is ~2s slower. Trade-offs?
maya: Good point. My proposal: primary enforcement at the router for p95 and error-rate (fast), enforcement at control plane for cost/quota decisions (useful for tenant budgets). Router should still accept a "skip-cost-check" header for internal traffic.
joel: Router-level guard needs to be cheap. Suggest a tiny rolling window: p95 over 1m + error > 2% triggers circuit for that route. For token cost, have control plane compute expected cost delta per minute and if exceeded, emit a pause.
anita: UX ask for console: when a rollout is paused, we need a visible card showing "pause reason" (latency/error/cost), a small timeline, and a one-click resume with explanation. Also show which policy triggered it (policy id).
luo: Implementation note: we'll need a deterministic tie-breaker if both router and control plane disagree (e.g., router says OK but control plane says pause for spend). I propose control plane decision wins and router caches a short TTL (10s) to avoid flipflop.
maya: Sounds reasonable. Also want an opt-in cost-estimator per-route so product owners can preview the cost impact of a traffic ramp. Could be a dry-run in console that simulates expected tokens * token_price.
joel: Here's a tiny example guard config I sketched: 
```json
{
  "guards": [
    {"type":"latency","p95_ms":350,"window_s":60},
    {"type":"error_rate","threshold_pct":2,"window_s":60},
    {"type":"cost_delta","max_usd_per_min":15,"evaluated_by":"control_plane"}
  ],
  "auto_pause": true,
  "resume_policy": "manual"
}
```
maya: Nice. For auto_pause=true, we should include a short grace period (3 failed minutes) before pausing to avoid noisy signals. Also log an event to ops-watchdog.
deploy-bot: Canary started: model v2 -> recommendations @ 10% traffic, started by maya at 1918004321.
ops-watchdog: Noted. If pause happens, will create incident stub and ping #eng-oncall.
joel: One more thing — telemetry: emit both aggregated and per-tenant metrics to the rollouts index. We'll need a dimension for "policy_id" and "decision_point" (router|control_plane). That will make debugging pauses straightforward.
anita: Agreed. Also add a small annotation on timeline entries linking to the evaluated input (request sample) for the failing window — obfuscated tokens.
maya: Great, can someone (joel/luo) own the router guard change? I'll take console bits (pause card + estimator). We'll reconvene after the first 30m.
luo: I'll take router. Will open a PR with a changelog and tests for the 1m p95 calc.
joel: I'll wire telemetry and the control-plane cost scorer.
maya: Thanks. If anything tripped, please ping me directly. :thumbsup:
